question: Do the Action Plan and the MPRs address all potential pollution contributors on the Kabini stretch?
intro: The Kabini's CPCB polluted stretch runs Nanjangud to Hejjige (Priority IV). This section compares the KSPCB Action Plan's commitments with what the monthly progress reports actually report. 'Not reported' means absent from the documents, not necessarily absent on the ground.

primary.label: NMCG Monthly Progress Report (Karnataka, Kabini stretch)
primary.note: June 2025 is the last stretch-wise MPR edition we hold for this stretch.

actionPlan.label: KSPCB Action Plan for Rejuvenation of River Kabini (mirrored)

baseline.banner: MPR editions from October 2025 onward no longer report stretch-wise status - accountability tracking anchors on the last stretch-wise reporting.
otherSources: CPCB Polluted River Stretches report (October 2025, mirrored)

solid-waste.label: NGT OA 606/2018 - SWM Rules compliance (Justice Subhash B Adi committee)

biomedical.label: NGT OA 710/2017 - BMW Rules 2016 (KSPCB guidelines hub)

fecal-sludge.label: SC (2017) 5 SCC 326 - mandatory sewage treatment infrastructure; NGT OA 673/2018 monitoring

public-stps.label: SC (2017) 5 SCC 326 - mandatory treatment infrastructure; NGT OA 673/2018 monthly reporting

effluent.label: Water Act consent regime; KSPCB hazardous waste management

regions.name: Nanjangud (CMC)
regions.inBasinNote: The stretch ULB - population 50,137; the temple town and its industrial belt sit at the head of the polluted reach.

categories.label: Public STPs

actionPlan.summary: 100% UGD for the entire town and a terminal STP treating to CPCB standards.

mpr.summary: One 7 MLD STP, operational and complied - but only 2 MLD utilised against 5.41 MLD generated (gap 3.41 MLD); 60% household connections done; Rs 36.86 crore DPR for the UGD network and SBT upgrade 'under completion stage' against a completion timeline of 31-03-2021.

gaps: The under-utilisation problem: capacity exists (7 MLD) but only 2 MLD reaches it - the network, not the plant, is the bottleneck, and the network timeline lapsed in March 2021.
'Under completion stage' repeats across editions with no percent-complete trail.

categories.label: Solid Waste

actionPlan.summary: The plan itself records ~20 TPD generation and that despite an MSW site existing, some waste is dumped on the river banks - with disposal only at the MSW site committed.

mpr.summary: 26 TPD generated; compost processing around 6 TPD; sanitary landfill and expanded processing 'under progress' via tendering.

gaps: Processing covers roughly a quarter of generation; the bank-dumping the plan acknowledged has no explicit closure status in the MPRs.
Bulk waste generators and waste destinations are not itemised.

categories.label: Biomedical Waste

actionPlan.summary: Biomedical waste does not appear in the Kabini Action Plan.
actionPlan.cite: Kabini Action Plan (full text, zero mentions)

mpr.summary: 0.217 kg/day reported across 35 bedded and 50 non-bedded health-care facilities; disposal via CBMWTF.

gaps: The reported generation figure (0.217 kg/day for 85 facilities) is implausibly low as stated - likely a units error in the MPR itself; no facility-level trail to check it against.

categories.label: Fecal Sludge

actionPlan.summary: Faecal sludge and septage do not appear in the Action Plan.

mpr.summary: With 40% of households unconnected to the UGD, their septage route is not reported in any edition.

gaps: The unsewered share's septage is the unaccounted flow between the town and the river.

mpr.summary: No private STP reporting for Nanjangud in any edition.

regions.name: Nanjangud industrial areas (KIADB, Thandya / Adakanahalli)
regions.inBasinNote: Sugar, distillery, steel, paper, pharmaceutical, food-processing and textile units concentrated in the taluk's industrial areas.

categories.label: Industrial effluent

actionPlan.summary: The plan asserts every industry in the taluk has an ETP, treats its effluent, and uses treated water on-land within premises - 'no industries are discharging into the river'.

mpr.summary: The zero-discharge position is carried forward in the progress reports.

gaps: The zero-discharge claim is the board's own assertion, unverified by any published effluent data - for a sugar/distillery/pharma cluster upstream of a Priority-IV stretch, that is the matrix's biggest open question.
No OCEMS-style public feed exists for these units to check the claim against.

regions.name: Gram Panchayats (Kabini stretch)
regions.inBasinNote: The rural reach between Nanjangud and Hejjige.
regions.silentNote: No MPR edition and no Action Plan item reports anything at gram-panchayat level for this stretch - the rural reach is unreported in the official accountability trail.
